name: What is the difference between porcelain tile and natural marble?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between porcelain tile and natural marble?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain tile is denser, less porous, and more scratch-resistant, making it ideal for heavy-traffic entryways and low-maintenance bathroom floors. Marble is a natural stone that offers distinct veining and classic luxury, but it is softer and porous. Marble requires regular sealing to resist stains and moisture, and it can etch if exposed to acidic cleaners. Porcelain offers easier long-term upkeep and consistent durability, while marble delivers a one-of-a-kind natural look that demands gentler cleaning routines and periodic resealing. Your choice comes down to whether you prioritize minimal maintenance or unique stone aesthetics.
acceptedAnswer.description: Porcelain is dense, highly stain-resistant, and low-maintenance, whereas natural marble offers unique veining but is porous, requiring regular sealing and gentler care.
